file 644 @S/units/own-ci-ci@.service
  | # Managed by the runner lanes kit (bin/provision-lane.sh); do not edit on the machine.
  | # One ci slot of the own-ci lane. The lane's listener (own-ci-listener.service) writes the slot's JIT
  | # config and job file under @S/run/ci/<n>/ and starts this unit for that one job; the
  | # container takes the job and exits, and the unit stays down until the listener starts it again.
  | # No [Install]: an instance started at boot would have no job to run. See README.md.
  | [Unit]
  | Description=own-ci lane ci slot %i (one disposable Sysbox container per job)
  | Requires=docker.service sysbox.service
  | After=docker.service sysbox.service network-online.target
  | Wants=network-online.target
  | RequiresMountsFor=@S/state @S/state/store
  | # Never refuse a start: the listener may start one instance several times a minute.
  | StartLimitIntervalSec=0
  | 
  | [Service]
  | Type=simple
  | Slice=own-ci.slice
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_NAME=own-ci
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_SCOPE=user
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_SLOT_GB=6
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_BRIDGE=own-ci0
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_GH_HOSTS=@S/state/home/.config/gh/hosts.yml
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_STATE_DIR=@S/state
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_STORE_DIR=@S/state/store
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_RUN_DIR=@S/run
  | # Each instance's 4-core set (systemd expands %i first, then ${KNOWN_CI_CPUSET_<n>}), so a job
  | # sees nproc=4 like a hosted runner.
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_CPUSET_1=0-3
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_CPUSET_2=4-7
  | # KNOWN_CI_IMAGE_TAG, written by bin/build-runner-image.sh; read at every start, so a rebuilt image
  | # (and its preloaded store, which prepare snapshots) is picked up by the next job without touching
  | # this unit.
  | EnvironmentFile=@S/state/image.env
  | ExecStartPre=+@ROOT/bin/lane-slot.sh prepare ci %i
  | ExecStart=/usr/bin/docker run --rm --runtime=sysbox-runc --network own-ci --cgroup-parent own-ci.slice --memory 4g --pids-limit 2048 --tmpfs /tmp:size=2g,exec --oom-score-adj 1000 --dns 1.1.1.1 --dns 8.8.8.8 --cpuset-cpus ${KNOWN_CI_CPUSET_%i} -v @S/state/slot-ci-%i:/home/runner -v @S/state/store/slot-ci-%i:/var/lib/docker -v @S/run/ci/%i/jit:/run/jit:ro --name own-ci-ci-%i own-ci-runner:${KNOWN_CI_IMAGE_TAG}
  | ExecStopPost=+@ROOT/bin/lane-slot.sh cleanup ci %i
  | # One job per start: the listener starts the next.
  | Restart=no
  | # runtime_max_sec, plus warm_max_age_sec for a lane with a warm pool: systemd counts it from the
  | # unit's start, and the listener recycles a warm slot once it has been up warm_max_age_sec, so a
  | # job the slot takes just before still has the whole runtime_max_sec.
  | RuntimeMaxSec=3600
  | # The slot helper's back-off sleeps up to ten minutes inside ExecStartPre.
  | TimeoutStartSec=15min
  | # Also the cleanup's budget (ExecStopPost). The cleanup renames the job's store into
  | # @S/state/store/trash for own-ci-store-reaper.service and deletes nothing of it; what can still take minutes is a
  | # qae store's lock (120 s) and a store the trash could not take, which is deleted here. Deleting one
  | # (270k files) took 20 to over 60 s on a loaded machine (2026-10-05), and at 60 s systemd killed 195
  | # of 332 cleanups, whose rm kept running beside the next job's snapshot on the same store.
  | TimeoutStopSec=300

file 644 @S/units/own-ci-qae@.service
  | # Managed by the runner lanes kit (bin/provision-lane.sh); do not edit on the machine.
  | # One qae slot of the own-ci lane. The lane's listener (own-ci-listener.service) writes the slot's JIT
  | # config and job file under @S/run/qae/<n>/ and starts this unit for that one job; the
  | # container takes the job and exits, and the unit stays down until the listener starts it again.
  | # No [Install]: an instance started at boot would have no job to run. See README.md.
  | [Unit]
  | Description=own-ci lane qae slot %i (one disposable Sysbox container per job)
  | Requires=docker.service sysbox.service
  | After=docker.service sysbox.service network-online.target
  | Wants=network-online.target
  | RequiresMountsFor=@S/state @S/state/store
  | # Never refuse a start: the listener may start one instance several times a minute.
  | StartLimitIntervalSec=0
  | 
  | [Service]
  | Type=simple
  | Slice=own-ci.slice
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_NAME=own-ci
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_SCOPE=user
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_SLOT_GB=6
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_BRIDGE=own-ci0
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_GH_HOSTS=@S/state/home/.config/gh/hosts.yml
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_STATE_DIR=@S/state
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_STORE_DIR=@S/state/store
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_RUN_DIR=@S/run
  | # One Codex login store per qae instance, mounted into that instance's QAE jobs only: Codex
  | # rotates a login's refresh token as a job uses it, so two concurrent jobs on one store would retire
  | # each other's session. systemd expands %i first, then ${KNOWN_CI_CODEX_STORE_<n>}; an instance
  | # beyond qae_concurrency has no store, and its prepare refuses. prepare resets the store to the
  | # login and the tracked config before every job, and cleanup gives it back to own-ci.
  | # The job holds the store's lock, @S/run/qae/<n>.codex.lock, for its whole run, as prepare and
  | # cleanup do while they touch the store, so own-ci-codex-keepalive.service never refreshes a login a job is
  | # using (bin/lane-slot.sh, "The Codex store lock"). flock -F executes docker run in its own place,
  | # so the unit's main process and exit status stay docker run's; it waits at most 60 s, though only
  | # the keepalive checking the instance (a moment) can hold the lock then.
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_CODEX_STORE_1=@S/state/codex
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_CODEX_CONFIG=@S/etc/own-ci/codex-config.toml
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_CODEX_OWNER=own-ci
  | # Each instance's 4-core set (systemd expands %i first, then ${KNOWN_CI_CPUSET_<n>}), so a job
  | # sees nproc=4 like a hosted runner.
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_CPUSET_1=0-3
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_CPUSET_2=4-7
  | # KNOWN_CI_IMAGE_TAG, written by bin/build-runner-image.sh; read at every start, so a rebuilt image
  | # (and its preloaded store, which prepare snapshots) is picked up by the next job without touching
  | # this unit.
  | EnvironmentFile=@S/state/image.env
  | ExecStartPre=+@ROOT/bin/lane-slot.sh prepare qae %i
  | ExecStart=/usr/bin/flock -F -w 60 @S/run/qae/%i.codex.lock /usr/bin/docker run --rm --runtime=sysbox-runc --network own-ci --cgroup-parent own-ci.slice --memory 4g --pids-limit 2048 --tmpfs /tmp:size=2g,exec --oom-score-adj 1000 --dns 1.1.1.1 --dns 8.8.8.8 --cpuset-cpus ${KNOWN_CI_CPUSET_%i} -v @S/state/slot-qae-%i:/home/runner -v @S/state/store/slot-qae-%i:/var/lib/docker -v @S/run/qae/%i/jit:/run/jit:ro -v ${KNOWN_CI_CODEX_STORE_%i}:/home/runner/.codex-qae --name own-ci-qae-%i own-ci-runner:${KNOWN_CI_IMAGE_TAG}
  | ExecStopPost=+@ROOT/bin/lane-slot.sh cleanup qae %i
  | # One job per start: the listener starts the next.
  | Restart=no
  | # runtime_max_sec, plus warm_max_age_sec for a lane with a warm pool: systemd counts it from the
  | # unit's start, and the listener recycles a warm slot once it has been up warm_max_age_sec, so a
  | # job the slot takes just before still has the whole runtime_max_sec.
  | RuntimeMaxSec=3600

  | TimeoutStartSec=15min
  | # Also the cleanup's budget (ExecStopPost). The cleanup renames the job's store into
  | # @S/state/store/trash for own-ci-store-reaper.service and deletes nothing of it; what can still take minutes is a
  | # qae store's lock (120 s) and a store the trash could not take, which is deleted here. Deleting one

  | # of 332 cleanups, whose rm kept running beside the next job's snapshot on the same store.
  | TimeoutStopSec=300
file 644 @S/units/own-ci-store-reaper.service
  | # Managed by the runner lanes kit (bin/provision-lane.sh); do not edit on the machine.
  | # The own-ci lane's store reaper (bin/lane-slot.sh reap): deletes the store copies its slots retired
  | # into @S/state/store/trash under one lock: one at a time, or a few at a time while the store is under
  | # pressure (REAP_JOBS in that script). Every slot's cleanup starts it without waiting (systemctl
  | # start --no-block), and own-ci-store-reaper.timer does, so no copy is left there by a start that was
  | # missed or by a reboot. No start timeout (a oneshot has none): emptying a backlog is its job, and a
  | # killed run would only begin again where it stopped. A run that never ends replaces itself now
  | # and then, between deletes, with the helper on disk (REAP_MAX_SEC there), so a pulled helper
  | # reaches it.
  | [Unit]
  | Description=own-ci lane: delete the store copies its slots retired
  | RequiresMountsFor=@S/state/store
  | # Never refuse a start: a cleanup starts it after every job, several times within seconds when jobs
  | # end together, and a refused start would leave a copy in the trash until the timer.
  | StartLimitIntervalSec=0
  | 
  | [Service]
  | Type=oneshot
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_NAME=own-ci
  | Environment=KNOWN_CI_STORE_DIR=@S/state/store
  | ExecStart=@ROOT/bin/lane-slot.sh reap
  | # The lowest CPU priority, so a delete yields to everything else it shares a core with. It runs
  | # outside own-ci.slice on purpose: the lane's CPUQuota and MemoryHigh throttle what is in the slice, and
  | # the one thing that gives the store its space back must not stall with the jobs that fill it.
  | Nice=19
file 644 @S/units/own-ci-store-reaper.timer
  | # Managed by the runner lanes kit (bin/provision-lane.sh); do not edit on the machine.
  | # A minute after boot, then every 5 minutes, counted from the reaper's last activation: the
  | # backstop for a copy no cleanup's start reached, not the reaper's usual trigger.
  | [Unit]
  | Description=own-ci lane: delete retired store copies, every 5 minutes
  | 
  | [Timer]
  | OnBootSec=1min
  | OnUnitActiveSec=5min
  | 
  | [Install]
  | WantedBy=timers.target
